title: Isolation of nuclei from mouse white adipose tissues for single-nucleus genomics
protocol: Transfer 400 mg of gonadal adipose tissue to a pre-cooled Petri dish on ice.
Mince the tissue thoroughly using a scalpel until less than 1 mm³ in size.
Add 500 μL of NIB to the minced tissue.
Transfer minced adipose tissue to a pre-cooled 2 mL glass Dounce homogenizer on ice.
Apply 5 strokes with pestle A to the tissue in the homogenizer.
Apply 5 strokes with pestle B to the tissue in the homogenizer.
Pre-wet a 70 μm cell strainer with DEPC-treated water.
Filter the homogenate through the pre-wetted cell strainer into a pre-cooled 50 mL tube on ice.
Wash the Dounce homogenizer with 1 mL NIB and filter through the same cell strainer.
Transfer the filtered homogenate to a pre-cooled 5 mL DNA Low binding tube on ice using a P1000 pipette.
Wash the cell strainer with 1 mL NIB and add to the filtered homogenate in the 5 mL tube to a total volume of approximately 2.5 mL using a P1000 pipette.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 1000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a fixed-angled rotor.
Aspirate the top lipid layer from the adipose tissue homogenate.
Resuspend the pellet in the remaining supernatant using a P1000 pipette.
Transfer the resuspended nuclei to a new pre-cooled 5 mL DNA Low binding tube on ice.
Wash the first 5 mL tube twice with 1 mL NIB.
Transfer any remaining nuclei from the washes to the new 5 mL tube containing the resuspended nuclei using a P1000 pipette.
Pellet the nuclei by centrifuging at 500×g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a swing-bucket rotor.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Use vacuum aspiration to remove most of the supernatant, leaving 80–100 μL.
Remove remaining supernatant with a P100 pipette.
Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 100 μL NRB by pipetting using a regular P1000 pipette.
Pre-wet a 40 μm tip strainer with NRB.
Filter the nuclei through the pre-wetted tip strainer using a P1000 pipette into a pre-cooled 1.5 mL DNA Low binding tube on ice.
Mix nuclei and Trypan Blue in equal ratio in a separate tube.
Transfer 10 μL of the nuclei-Trypan Blue solution to the Bürker counting chamber.
Count at least 3 squares using bright-field microscopy.
Quantify the nuclei concentration using the formula: Nuclei mL = (∑ nuclei count in n squares / (n × 10^4)) × 2
Take out 12,000 nuclei and resuspend in Nuclei Recovery Buffer (NRB) to a total volume of 43.2 μL.
Resuspend the mixture on ice in a new pre-cooled 1.5 mL DNA low binding tube.
Load nuclei into the 10× Genomics Chromium Controller.
Run according to manufacturer recommendations for steps 1 and 2.
Prepare dual-indexed paired-end sequencing libraries for Illumina sequencing.
Perform sample index PCR using half sample volumes with a total reaction volume of 50 μL.
Store remaining samples at −20°C for up to a month if needed.
Sequence each library using an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 sequencer.
Aim for read coverage of 30,000–50,000 read pairs per droplet (totaling 250 million reads).
